PortBinding.description: A port of the container and where it is published.

published.description: `127.0.0.1:8080`, `[::]:8080`; empty when the port is only exposed.

PositionRange.description: An inclusive range of offsets or sequences, as decimal strings.

QueryInput.description:
`messaging.query`: a jq program on a JSON value the UI shows (the message detail's Query bar
and Profile, spec §5.6), run in a worker with the limits of §5.4.1.

jq.description: A jq program, run by jaq.

text.description: The value's JSON text, at most 8 MiB.

timeoutMs.description: The deadline in milliseconds (the user's setting); 2 s when absent, clamped to 0.5 to 30 s.

bytes.description: The results' JSON text, in bytes.

stopped.description: Why the run returned before the program ended: the 1 MiB cap, or the deadline.

ReadValueInput.description: What `langgraph.threads.readValue` reads: one value of a checkpoint or of a run, whole.

checkpointId.description: The checkpoint (the current state when absent).

runId.description: A run's value (`metadata`, `request.input`); when absent, a checkpoint's.

RecordHeader.description: One header of a [`MessageRecord`]; names repeat when the system allows several values.

RecordHeaderEncoding.description: How a header value travels: as text when it is valid UTF-8, else as base64.

RecoveryCodes.description: Output of `app.account.totp.confirm`: the recovery codes, shown once.

RegistryAuthKind.description: How the server authenticates to the registry.

RegistryProfile.description:
The profile's registry (`fields.schemaRegistry` with its secrets), as a tool's connect input
and `messaging.registry.test` take it.

tls.description:
The CA to trust for `https` (no system roots), the server name to check, and a client
certificate for mutual TLS (its key a secret).

wireFormatSubjects.description:
NATS: the subject patterns whose messages may carry the Confluent wire format, which
auto-detect looks for there only. Absent: everywhere (Kafka).

RegistryRef.description: A schema in the registry, by id or by subject and version.

registry.description: The profile's registry as saved; `null` removes it.

RegistryTestOutput.description: What a registry said when tested.

compatibility.description: The global compatibility level; absent when the registry does not say.

mode.description: `READWRITE`, `READONLY`, `IMPORT`; absent when the registry does not say.

RelationChild.description: A child started by this run, from its history.

failure.description: The failure's message, or why it could not start.

status.description: `Running` once started; `Unspecified` while only initiated or when it could not start.

RelationEdge.description: An arrow: parent to child, or the sender of a signal or cancel to its target.

eventId.description: The event of this run that records it.

RelationFamily.description: What the server can say about the family, and how much of it is drawn.

drawn.description: Boxes drawn in the tree (the other ends of signals not counted).

notDrawn.description: Workflows of the family left out of the drawing.

query.description:
The Workflows query that lists the scope's workflows; absent when the server has no
attribute for it.

reason.description: Why Whole family is not offered: the server's answer.

scope.description: The scope the answer is for (`direct` when the server cannot list the family).

supported.description: The server's visibility knows `RootWorkflowId` (Temporal Server 1.24 and later).

total.description: Workflows in the family (every run), as the server counts them; absent when unsupported.

RelationNode.description: One box of the graph: a workflow, by its ID (its latest run seen).

failure.description: The failure's message, for a failed child (from this run's history).

level.description:
Depth below the top drawn level (0); absent for a workflow outside the tree (the other end
of a signal or cancel).

missing.description: Gone from the server (past retention, or never started).

runId.description: Empty when only the workflow ID is known (a child that did not start).

RelationParent.description: The parent, with what happens to this child when it closes (while the child is pending in it).

RelationRuns.description: The run's place in its chain of runs.

continuedAs.description: The run that continued this one.

continuedFrom.description: The run this one continued from (continue-as-new, retry or cron).

firstRunId.description: The first run of the chain, when it is another run.

resetFrom.description: The run this one was reset from.

resetTo.description: The latest run made by resetting this one.

RelationScope.description: Whole family (every workflow under the root) or Direct only (one level each way).

RelationSignal.description: A signal or cancel between this run and another workflow, from this run's history.

outcome.description: For a sent one: `Delivered`, `Failed: <cause>`, or absent while in flight.

RemoteError.description: The target's own error code, for Details.

code.description: Kafka error name, gRPC status, HTTP status, Kubernetes `Status.reason`, NATS error code.

ResetReapply.description: Which signals a reset re-applies to the new run.

oneOf.description: Every eligible event after the reset point (signals and updates).

RetryPolicyForm.description: A retry policy; empty fields take the server's defaults.

cuts.description: The values this reply left out (`metadata`, `request.input`), each over its share (TSK-108).

request.description:
What the run was asked to do, from its `kwargs`: only `runs.get` sends it (TSK-96), so a
list of runs stays light.

RunCommand.description: `Command` of a run: resume an interrupt, update the state, go to a node.

goto.description: A node name, or a list of them.

RunLink.description: Another run of the same workflow ID, and why it exists.

RunRequest.description:
A run's request as the server keeps it in the run's `kwargs` (TSK-96: "Run again with the same
input"). Each part is absent when the server did not keep it.

input.description: The graph's input; `null` for a run that resumed or continued without one.

lastEventId.description: The id of the last event forwarded (for `langgraph.runs.join`).

status.description: The run's status when its stream ended (`success`, `error`, `interrupted`, ...).

lastEventId.description:
The id of the last event seen: the stream resumes after it. From the run's current
event when absent; `-1` replays the run from its start.

offset.description: The runs to skip: the `next` of the previous page.

RunsPage.description: A page of a thread's runs: at most about 4 MiB, whatever `limit` says (TSK-108).

items.description: Newest first. A run's metadata over its share is `null` with a note in its `cuts`.

next.description: Pass it as `offset` for the next page; absent when the runs end here.

assistantId.description: An assistant id or a graph id.

interruptBefore.description: Node names, or `["*"]` for every node.

multitaskStrategy.description: `reject`, `rollback`, `interrupt` or `enqueue` when the thread is busy.

threadId.description: The thread to run on; `null` for a run without a thread.

scheduledTime.description: When it should have run, RFC 3339.

status.description: `Running`, `Completed`, ... as the workflow's status, when the server says it.

args.description:
One `json/plain` payload per argument. A described schedule whose input is not JSON has
`{ "$opaque": … }` values here, which an update refuses until they are replaced.

workflowId.description: Temporal appends the scheduled time to it.

endTime.description: RFC 3339, after the start and not in the future.

overlap.description: The schedule's own policy when absent.

ScheduleDetail.description: Everything `DescribeSchedule` says; the parts are protobuf JSON, payloads decoded.

action.description: `schedule.action`: the workflow it starts (type, id, task queue, input).

conflictToken.description: Sent back by `update` so a concurrent change is a conflict, not lost.

form.description: The schedule as the edit sheet fills it (TSK-92).

info.description: `info`: action counts, running workflows, create and update times.

policies.description: `schedule.policies`: overlap, catch-up window, pause on failure.

spec.description: `schedule.spec`: intervals, calendars, cron strings, jitter, time zone.

ScheduleForm.description: A schedule as the sheet edits it.

ScheduleOverlap.description: What to do when a triggered run meets one that is still running.

note.description: The note shown with the pause or unpause.

overlap.description: For `trigger`: the schedule's own policy when absent.

catchupWindow.description: How late a missed run may still start; one year when absent.

ScheduleRun.description: One row of a schedule's Runs: a workflow it started, or a time it matched with no run.

scheduledTime.description: The time the spec called for (`TemporalScheduledStartTime`); for Trigger now, the trigger.

skipped.description: A matched time with no run: why, as far as it can be told.

query.description: The Workflows query the runs come from.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone; UTC when absent.

remainingActions.description: Runs left before the schedule stops by itself; unlimited when absent.

notes.description: The note of the last pause or unpause.

endTime.description:
RFC 3339; when absent, the range grows from `startTime` until `limit` times are found
(at most five years ahead).

limit.description: At most this many times: 20 when absent, 1,000 at most.

truncated.description: More times matched than were sent.

conflictToken.description: For `update`: the token of the `describe` the sheet was filled from.

query.description: A schedule visibility query; every schedule when empty.

SchemaFile.description: One source file of a local schema.

SchemaIssue.description: A problem found compiling a schema, with the file and line when known (spec §5.3).

schemaId.description: The local schema's id, when the issue is about one.

SchemaMapping.description:
A codec, with a local schema when it needs one, mapped to messages (spec §4.2,
`extras.mappings`); the first mapping that matches a message wins.

codec.description: The codec; the schema's when absent (mappings saved before CBOR name a schema only).

registry.description:
A schema from the profile's registry instead of a local one: a subject and version, or
an id. With neither, a `confluent` mapping takes the id each message carries.

schemaId.description: The local schema, for Avro, Protobuf and JSON Schema; none for the codecs without one.

wireFormat.description:
`confluent`: the bytes start with the wire format's magic byte and schema id (and, for
Protobuf, the message indexes), which are skipped. Raw bytes when absent.

SchemaRef.description: Where a schema comes from (spec §5.7): `{ registry: … }` or `{ local: schemaId }`.

SchemaStatus.description: A local schema in use on a connection.

messageTypes.description: Protobuf: the message types offered; empty for the other types.

SchemaVersion.description: A registry schema version: a number or `"latest"`.

SchemasStatusOutput.description: What a connection's codecs hold now (the Schemas tab).

issues.description: Schemas that do not compile, with file and line.

mappings.description: Every mapping, in order, with what it decoded.

registryUrl.description: The registry the connection uses, if any.

schemas.description: The schemas that compiled, in id order.

issues.description: Schemas that do not compile, with file and line; the others are in use.

SearchAttribute.description: One attribute a query can name.

custom.description: Registered for the namespace by its users, not built in.

SearchAttributeType.description: The value type of a search attribute (`IndexedValueType`).

SearchAttributesOutput.description: The namespace's attributes: custom ones first, then the built-in ones, each by name.

fallback.description: Set when the server did not list them and these are the built-in ones only: its message.

error.description: Why the queue could not be described.

SshFacts.description: The connection's SSH side, for the Host page's subtitle.

StandaloneActivitiesSupport.description:
Whether the server runs standalone activities on the profile's namespace (`temporal.connect`'s
capabilities, from a `CountActivityExecutions` at connect).

StateTask.description: A task of the next step: the node to run, its error, its interrupts.

state.description: A subgraph task's own state (when asked for subgraphs).

Stopped.description: Why a run returned before its program ended.

oneOf.description: The next result would have passed 1 MiB of JSON text.
The deadline passed; the results are those that arrived before it.

score.description: Relevance of a semantic search hit.

filter.description: Items whose value has these fields and values.

query.description: Natural-language query (semantic search, when the store has an index).

TailSummary.description: The summary of a message stream (spec §5.5, `TailSummary`).

filterError.description:
Why the filter's jq last failed on a message (its error, or the limit that stopped it);
such a message counts in `decodeErrors`.

Target.description:
Where a message lives, for mappings and subject naming: a Kafka topic, a NATS subject (core
or JetStream) or a KV bucket.

oneOf.description: A NATS subject; `stream` when the message was read from a JetStream stream.

workflowBacklog.description: Tasks waiting for a poller, when the server reports it.

TaskQueueSource.description: Where a task queue was found.

TemporalCapabilities.description: What the server reports about itself.

standaloneActivities.description: Whether the profile's namespace runs standalone activities (TSK-92), and why not.

visibilityStore.description:
Which store holds visibility (`cassandra`, `mysql8`, `postgres12`, `sqlite`,
`elasticsearch`, ...); empty when the cluster did not say. Cassandra has basic visibility
only, so the list's query bar is limited (spec §9.3).

clusterName.description: The cluster's name, when it reported one.

TemporalTestCodecInput.description:
"Test codec" in the profile sheet: the draft profile, and the namespace to sample (the
profile's when empty).

TemporalTestCodecOutput.description: What the codec did with the inputs of the namespace's latest workflows.

error.description: Why the codec failed, when it did.

workflowIds.description: The workflows sampled (their inputs' first payload).

TemporalTlsOptions.description:
TLS settings of a profile (spec §4.2 `TemporalTlsOptions`); `secrets.clientKeyPem` comes beside it as
`clientKeyPem`. There is no "skip verification" (spec Open question 6).

caPem.description: Extra trusted CA certificates (PEM); the operating system's roots are used as well.

serverName.description: The name to verify the server certificate against, when it is not the address's host.

data.description: The bytes typed or pasted, base64; at most 64 KiB decoded.

before.description: Checkpoints older than this one (the next page).

metadata.description:
Only the checkpoints whose metadata holds these pairs, e.g. `{ "run_id": … }` for one run's
steps (TSK-96). An object.

ThreadHistoryPage.description: A page of the history: at most about 4 MiB, whatever `limit` says (TSK-108).

items.description: Newest first. A value over its share is `null` with a note in the item's `cuts`.

next.description: Pass it as `before` for the next page; absent when the history ends here.

ThreadState.description: A thread's state at a checkpoint (`GET /threads/{id}/state`, one entry of the history).

cuts.description:
The values this reply left out, each over its share of the reply's bytes (TSK-108): the
field is `null` here and the cut says what it was. Empty when nothing was cut.

interrupts.description: Every pending interrupt of the state, its tasks' included.

next.description: The nodes the next step runs; empty when the graph has ended.

checkpointId.description: The state at this checkpoint (time travel); the current state when absent.

full.description:
Allow the reply to weigh up to 12 MiB instead of 8 MiB, to load a value that came back
cut (`cuts`); over that, `threads.readValue` streams it.

subgraphs.description: Include the subgraphs' states in the tasks.

TimeRange.description: An inclusive range of RFC 3339 times.

TlsOptions.description:
TLS settings of a profile, as `toConnect` sends them (spec §4.2). `clientKeyPem` comes from
the profile's `secrets`; procedures that take it list it in `redact`.

caPem.description: PEM certificates of the CA to trust instead of the system's trust store.

clientCertPem.description: PEM client certificate (chain) for mutual TLS.

clientKeyPem.description: PEM private key of the client certificate. A secret.

enabled.description: Use TLS. Tools whose address says it (`https://`) use TLS either way.

serverName.description: The name the server's certificate must carry, when it is not the address's host.

field.description: For `Invalid`: the input field at fault, as the UI names it.

hostKey.description: For `HostKey`: what the trust dialog shows.

position.description: For `Invalid`: where in the field's text, when known.

system.description: The tool id (`nats`, `kafka`, `k8s`, ...), or `app` for shared procedures.

ToolErrorKind.description: What went wrong, as the UI needs to know it (spec §2.6).

oneOf.description: The target refused, timed out or is unreachable.
The target rejected the credentials.
The TLS handshake or verification failed.
The SSH host key is unknown or changed.
The target denied the operation (ACL, RBAC, permissions).
The named resource does not exist, or the `connId` is gone (`resource = "connection"`).
Exists already, wrong revision, not empty, not running.
Input the target or a codec rejected.
Any other target error, with its native code in `remote`.

ToolInfo.description: A tool built into the server.

version.description: The version of the tool's main library, or of the server for built-in samples.

code.description: The six-digit code the authenticator shows.

qrSvg.description: Its QR code as an SVG image (no script), made on the server.

uri.description: The `otpauth://totp/…` URI an authenticator app reads.

oneOf.description: [`MAX_ENTRIES`] entries were listed.
[`MAX_READ`] bytes were read (the folder holds large files).

asNode.description: The node the update is made as (the graph continues from its edges).

checkpointId.description: Update the state at this checkpoint, which forks a new branch from it.

values.description: The values to write, as a node's update.

ValueCut.description: A value that was left out of a reply because it was over its share.

bytes.description: Its size as compact JSON text.

preview.description: The first characters of its JSON text.

ValueStub.description:
Mounts the tool's APIs.
A value read whole and kept on the server for the large-state tree (TSK-96): what the UI's
payload view reads (Temporal's large-payload stub, with `json/plain` as its encoding).

bytes.description: Its compact JSON text, in bytes.

preview.description: The first 64 KiB of its indented JSON text.

project.description: The Compose project that made it.

size.description: Bytes on disk, from `/system/df`; absent when Docker did not say.

usedBy.description: Containers that mount it, stopped ones too.

sizeError.description: Why there are no sizes, when `/system/df` failed.

WireFormat.description: Whether encoding writes the Confluent wire format (spec §5.3).

WorkerRow.description: One worker on one task queue.

buildId.description: The build id it reports (worker versioning or deployment options).

lastAccessTime.description: Its latest poll on either kind, RFC 3339.

ratePerSecond.description: Tasks per second over both kinds, as the server measures it.

taskQueues.description: Task queues to describe besides the ones seen.

truncated.description: More task queues were seen than one call describes (50); typed ones come first.

autoResetPoints.description: `ResetPointInfo[]`: the points the server can reset to by itself.

historySizeBytes.description: The history's size in bytes, as the server counts it (TSK-92; Temporal's limit is 50 MiB).

memo.description: The memo's fields by name, decoded.

pendingActivities.description: `PendingActivityInfo[]`: type, state, attempt, last failure, heartbeat details, times.

searchAttributes.description: The search attributes by name, decoded.

pageSize.description:
At most this many events, 1 to 1,000; 1,000 when absent. A page also stops at 4 MiB of
reply (TSK-109).

reverse.description: Newest first (`GetWorkflowExecutionHistoryReverse`); oldest first when absent.

args.description: Each argument is sent as one `json/plain` payload.

queryType.description: `__stack_trace`, or a query the workflow defines.

result.description: The result payloads decoded: the value when there is one, an array of them otherwise.

WorkflowRawEventInput.description: One event of a run, to read as stored.

WorkflowRawEventOutput.description: An event's attributes as stored: protobuf JSON with each payload's `metadata` and `data` in base64.

reason.description: Required to terminate; optional to ask for cancellation.

WorkflowRef.description: Names a workflow run: the run id is the latest run when absent.

scope.description: `family` when absent; a server without `RootWorkflowId` answers as `direct`.

eventId.description: The event to reset to: a WorkflowTaskCompleted, WorkflowTaskStarted or failed task event.

WorkflowRow.description: One row of the workflow list.

durationMs.description: Close (or now, while running) minus start, in milliseconds, as the server reports it.

args.description: Each argument is sent as one `json/plain` payload.

started.description: False when the conflict policy UseExisting returned the running workflow instead.

WorkflowStatus.description: The execution status of a workflow (`WorkflowExecutionStatus`).

WorkflowsCountOutput.description: The number of workflows a query matches.

query.description:
A visibility query (`WorkflowType = "Order" AND ExecutionStatus = "Running"`); every
workflow when empty.

Xray.description: How deep to draw subgraphs: `true` all the way, a number that many levels, `false` none.
